Same files per shard in both runs (same product code); summed per-test time of the identical files rose 1.58x (shard 1) and 1.70x (shard 2) vs run 1 while shard 3 fell to 0.87x, and the unrelated Unit job's identical 97 files rose 1.87x (61 s -> 111 s step). The run-2 spread is runner speed variance, not assignment imbalance; judged PASS under the orchestrator's instruction to use step-level times, with finding J-1-01 recorded. Wall time on main and AC#3 remain for the post-merge measurement (Q-1).

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected the longest sweep job to be at most 1.5x the shortest on each branch run; actual run 46053833069 shows 171 s vs 94 s (1.82x), step 156 s vs 81 s. The same files took 1.6-1.9x longer per test on the shard 1/2 and Unit runners than in run 46052341998, so the cause is runner speed, which the weighted split cannot control.
findings.fix: No code change required. In the post-merge main measurement (Q-1), record sweep job and step times with per-test totals; if the raw ratio again exceeds ~1.5x on main with similar runner-normalised loads, treat it as runner noise, otherwise refresh weights.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected wall <= 210 s; actual 187 s and 204 s, with E2E (webkit, shard 2 of 2) at 184-200 s as the critical path, leaving ~6 s headroom on the slower run.
findings.fix: None now; spec Scope concerns already name 3 shards per browser or CI workers as the next lever if main exceeds ~3.5 min.
